title: Right-derived comparison unit for an exact coefficient square
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal A',\mathcal B,\mathcal B'$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], with ordinary unbounded derived categories and localization functors $Q$ from their homotopy categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume every complex of $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal A'$ admits a quasi-isomorphism to a K-injective complex, where K-injective means that every map from an acyclic complex is null-homotopic. Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and $G:\mathcal A'\to\mathcal B'$ be additive functors [def-sp-left-exact-additive], and let $U:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A'$ and $V:\mathcal B\to\mathcal B'$ be exact additive functors. Fix a natural isomorphism $c:VF\xrightarrow{\sim}GU$. Use their termwise actions on complexes, exact descents $D(U),D(V)$ [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], and total right derived pairs $(RF,\eta^F),(RG,\eta^G)$ [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Then $D(V)RF$, with unit $D(V)(\eta^F)$, is a total right derived functor of $QVF$. There is a unique natural transformation $\gamma:D(V)RF\to RG D(U)$ satisfying, for every complex $P$ of $\mathcal A$,
$$\gamma_{QP}\,D(V)(\eta^F_P)=\eta^G_{UP}\,Q(c_P).$$
All expressions use the canonical exact-functor localization identifications. Neither preservation of K-injectives by $U$ nor invertibility of $\gamma$ is assumed.

proof.text: Put $Q=Q_{\mathcal A}$, $H=D(V)RF$ and $E=Q_{\mathcal B'}V_KF_K$. The natural localization identification for the exact functor $V$ in [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] identifies $E$ with $D(V)Q_{\mathcal B}F_K$. Whiskering the supplied unit gives a natural transformation $\alpha:E\to HQ$. By the K-injective computation clause of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], $\eta^F_I$ is invertible for each K-injective $I$; hence $\alpha_I=D(V)(\eta^F_I)$ is invertible. We prove the universal property of $(H,\alpha)$ directly, retaining the canonical localization identifications throughout.

source.place: Tags 070I (lemma-K-injective) and 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined); explicit agent proof of postcomposition universality and comparison-unit consequence.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-localization-essentially-surjective], for every $X\in D(\mathcal A)$ choose a representative $P_X$ and an isomorphism $X\cong QP_X$. Choose a K-injective resolution $P_X\to I_X$ by hypothesis, and let $e_X:X\xrightarrow{\sim}QI_X$ be their composite. For every $a:X\to Y$, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] gives a unique homotopy-class map $f:I_X\to I_Y$ such that $Q(f)=e_Y a e_X^{-1}$. This uses K-injectivity of the target $I_Y$ and places no condition on the image under $U$ of any complex.

source.place: Tags 070I (lemma-K-injective) and 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined); explicit agent proof of postcomposition universality and comparison-unit consequence.

proof.text:
Let $T:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B')$ be any functor and $\tau:E\to TQ$ any natural transformation. Define
$$\beta_X=T(e_X)^{-1}\tau_{I_X}\alpha_{I_X}^{-1}H(e_X).$$
To check naturality, use the lift $f$ of $a:X\to Y$ from step 2. Naturality of $\alpha$ and $\tau$ gives $\alpha_{I_Y}^{-1}H(Qf)=E(f)\alpha_{I_X}^{-1}$ and $\tau_{I_Y}E(f)=T(Qf)\tau_{I_X}$. Consequently
$$\begin{aligned}\beta_YH(a)&=T(e_Y)^{-1}\tau_{I_Y}\alpha_{I_Y}^{-1}H(Qf)H(e_X)\\&=T(e_Y)^{-1}T(Qf)\tau_{I_X}\alpha_{I_X}^{-1}H(e_X)\\&=T(a)\beta_X,\end{aligned}$$
where the last equality uses $Qf=e_Yae_X^{-1}$. Thus $\beta:H\to T$ is natural.

source.place: Tags 070I (lemma-K-injective) and 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined); explicit agent proof of postcomposition universality and comparison-unit consequence.

proof.text:
For every complex $P$, the Hom bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], now with source $P$ and target $I_{QP}$, lifts $e_{QP}:QP\to QI_{QP}$ to a homotopy-class map $t:P\to I_{QP}$ with $Q(t)=e_{QP}$. Naturality gives $H(Qt)\alpha_P=\alpha_{I_{QP}}E(t)$ and $\tau_{I_{QP}}E(t)=T(Qt)\tau_P$. Substituting into step 3 yields
$$\beta_{QP}\alpha_P=T(e_{QP})^{-1}\tau_{I_{QP}}E(t)=\tau_P.$$
Hence composition with $\alpha$ is surjective on the stated natural-transformation sets.

source.place: Tags 070I (lemma-K-injective) and 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined); explicit agent proof of postcomposition universality and comparison-unit consequence.

proof.text:
If $\beta':H\to T$ also satisfies $\beta'_{QP}\alpha_P=\tau_P$ for all $P$, evaluating at $I_X$ gives $\beta'_{QI_X}=\tau_{I_X}\alpha_{I_X}^{-1}$. Naturality at $e_X$ forces
$$\beta'_X=T(e_X)^{-1}\tau_{I_X}\alpha_{I_X}^{-1}H(e_X)=\beta_X.$$
Thus composition with $\alpha$ is injective as well. Steps 3--5 establish its bijectivity for every $T$, exactly the universal property of a total right derived pair. They also show that changing the auxiliary choices gives the same transformation.

source.place: Tags 070I (lemma-K-injective) and 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined); explicit agent proof of postcomposition universality and comparison-unit consequence.

proof.text: Take $T=RG D(U)$. The localization identification for exact $U$ in [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] identifies $TQ$ with $RG Q_{\mathcal A'}U_K$. Degreewise $c$ and the natural unit of $RG$ from [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] therefore give a natural transformation $\tau:E\to TQ$ whose component is $\tau_P=\eta^G_{UP}Q(c_P)$. Apply the bijection proved in steps 3--5 to obtain the unique $\gamma:H\to RG D(U)$ with $\gamma_{QP}\alpha_P=\tau_P$. Since $\alpha_P=D(V)(\eta^F_P)$, this is precisely the required equation for every complex $P$.
